checks.name: token_verification_rejections
checks.reason: 28 tests. Real RS256 signatures from a real JWKS served over real HTTP. Refused: foreign issuer, foreign audience, expired, nbf in the future, alg=none, HS256-over-the-public-key (algorithm confusion, with a non-vacuity check that the HMAC is genuinely valid), wrong key under a published kid, unpublished and unknown kid, missing kid, forged typ, unknown crit, nonce mismatch, foreign azp with multi-valued aud, non-UUID subject, each missing claim, absent required scope, garbage input. Also: discovery document with a foreign issuer, non-https JWKS URL, and key rotation picked up without a restart.

checks.name: session_and_login_state_durability
checks.runtime: cloud-workspace/PG16.2 (real DDL from 0003, runtime role kb_app)
checks.reason: 24 tests against real PostgreSQL 16.2 on a dedicated kb_identity database, connecting as the unprivileged kb_app role. A login opened on one SessionStore is completed by a different one; state replay, wrong browser binding, expiry, forged and malformed cookies are all refused; a session row cannot be turned back into a cookie; no token column exists; a session with no account raises instead of inventing a UUID; idle and absolute deadlines, revocation and purge retention hold; kb_worker is refused SELECT; and a session principal sets the C06 transaction-local GUC that RLS then reads, which does not survive the transaction.

checks.name: browser_flow_pkce_cookies_csrf_two_gateways
checks.runtime: cloud-workspace/PG16.2 + local OIDC provider process (NOT Keycloak)
checks.reason: 30 tests over a real FastAPI app and real HTTP. Login redirects with response_type=code, S256 (never plain), state and nonce; the callback completes on a DIFFERENT gateway instance and the next request is served there (acceptance #3, S01); a replayed callback, a callback without the browser binding, and a token signed by the wrong key are refused; the session cookie is HttpOnly and the CSRF cookie deliberately is not; in production both carry the __Host- prefix and Secure; a write is refused with no CSRF token, with a header/cookie mismatch, and with an attacker-chosen pair, and succeeds with the matching one; x-user-id / x-forwarded-user / x-remote-user and a user_id in the body change nothing; logout revokes; no token, code, cookie value or client secret appears in any response body, and none appears in the log even with the root logger at DEBUG.

checks.name: realm_template_contains_no_secret
checks.reason: 3 of 9 tests in this file ran: the realm JSON parses, every credential field is a ${VAR} placeholder, the client is confidential with PKCE S256 and no implicit flow, no direct access grants, no service account, no users, registrationAllowed false, accessTokenLifespan <= 600, and the env template is placeholders on two distinct origins. The other 6 are skipped, not passed.

checks.name: full_integration_suite
checks.reason: 100 passed, 6 skipped, 16 deselected (exit 0). 85 of those are new C07 tests; 15 are the existing C03/C06 tests, which still pass with 0003 applied to the shared database. The 6 skips are the Keycloak leg and are reported as skipped in the pytest summary, not silently.

checks.name: check_and_self_test
checks.reason: ruff check + ruff format --check + mypy clean on 16 source files; 16 unit tests green; the injected defect is still rejected, so the gate is non-vacuous.

checks.reason: No Keycloak in this environment: no JVM, no keycloak binary (docs/handoff/runtime-capabilities.json keycloak_real.available=false). The six tests in test_keycloak_live.py that would need it are present and SKIPPED, never passed. Owner gate E03.

checks.reason: Unverified against the real provider: realm import, interactive login, TOTP/MFA, a second realm in the same Keycloak sharing a key set, password-grant refusal at the server, and backchannel logout revoking local sessions. The local stand-in in tests/integration/identity/conftest.py exercises the OIDC wire behaviour only and is NOT Keycloak.

checks.name: session_survives_a_real_gateway_restart
checks.reason: Needs a deployed gateway: no Podman and no systemd in this workspace (runtime-capabilities.json), and no live Keycloak either. The same property IS covered in-process by test_the_callback_and_the_next_request_work_through_another_gateway and test_a_session_survives_the_gateway_that_created_it, which use two independent SessionStore objects with separate connections; what they do not do is kill a real process. Owner gates E01 + E03.

checks.reason: Not a C07 gate and not a C07 change: no acceptance-marked test exists in the tree, and `just acceptance` exits 5 by design (C01 made a missing mandatory check non-zero). checks.name: authlib_for_the_token_exchange
checks.reason: Proposal for the lockfile owner, not a check. Authlib would own the authorization-code exchange and the PKCE bookkeeping more completely than PyJWT + httpx do. It is absent from requirements.lock and pyproject.toml, and this card is not allowed to edit either (AGENTS.md names a single owner for lockfiles). Installing it into the venv would make this tree pass locally and break for every other executor, so it was not done. If added, only src/kb/http/auth_flow.py changes.

blockers: Keycloak is absent from this environment (no JVM), so the provider half of C07 acceptance is unverified: realm import, interactive login, MFA, a second realm sharing a key set, password-grant refusal and backchannel logout. The six tests that would cover it are in tests/integration/identity/test_keycloak_live.py and are SKIPPED, not passed.

No Podman/systemd here, so deploy/identity/verify-session-durability.sh (restart a real gateway process) could not run. The equivalent property is proven in-process by two independent SessionStore objects; a real process kill is not.

Authlib is not in requirements.lock/pyproject.toml and this card may not edit lockfiles, so the token exchange is httpx over the PyJWT-verified ID token. Proposal for the lockfile owner, recorded under checks.authlib_for_the_token_exchange.
